text.arabic_uthmani: وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوٓا۟ أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ كَسَرَابٍۭ بِقِيعَةٍۢ يَحْسَبُهُ ٱلظَّمْـَٔانُ مَآءً حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَهُۥ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْـًۭٔا وَوَجَدَ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ فَوَفَّىٰهُ حِسَابَهُۥ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَرِيعُ ٱلْحِسَابِ

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction opening a contrastive parable while still linked to the prior reward unit
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) opens the ayah as a marked turn: the discourse remains connected to the preceding reward passage, but it launches a fresh counter-image. After light and provision without reckoning (24:35-38), this particle moves the reader into mirage, exposure, and swift reckoning.

topics.headline: contrastive parable opening
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah starts as a connected but fresh counter-image, not as a flat continuation.
topics.reason: The opening conjunction is licensed as resumptive and coordinating, opening a new parabolic unit while still linked to the previous passage.

topics.headline: light-to-mirage boundary
topics.reader_payoff: The reader sees the turn from rewarded light and unreckoned provision (24:35-38) into mirage and swift reckoning (24:39).
topics.reason: The rows give the boundary payoff with concrete references, so the prose keeps the shift from 24:35-38 to 24:39 explicit.

words.gloss_range: definite masculine plural relative pronoun making a class-defining topic
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلَّذِينَ}} ({{tr:alladhīna}}) names no individuals; it forms a recognizable class through the following action. The fronted relative phrase restarts reference after the believer chain of 24:38, so the evaluation of deeds begins under a new, action-defined heading.

topics.headline: class formed by relative clause
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the group is identified by its defining action before its deeds are evaluated.
topics.reason: The relative pronoun forms the nominative topic with the following verb, making the action the criterion for the group.

topics.headline: fronted restart after believer chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a new class replacing the previous believer pronoun-chain, sharpening the adjacent contrast with 24:38.
topics.reason: The rows preserve the word order and boundary contrast: the class is fronted before the deeds predicate and restarts reference after 24:38.

words.gloss_range: Form I perfect plural disbelief/rejection, locally objectless and class-defining
words.root_gloss_range: covering, concealment, ingratitude, and disbelief; locally the theological rejection sense is selected while covering remains image pressure
words.prose: {{ar:كَفَرُوٓا۟}} ({{tr:kafarū}}) presents the class-defining rejection as already settled and objectless: the ayah does not limit it to denial of one named object. The root’s covering pressure is realized by the mirage scene, where false appearance conceals absence until exposure; even the sower/seed covering image is inverted on barren terrain into non-fruition. It also joins the familiar voided-deeds pattern, with disbelieving works pictured as ashes (14:18), weightless loss (18:103-105), and here mirage.

topics.headline: settled objectless disbelief
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices disbelief presented as an established, direct condition rather than a one-object dispute or ongoing process.
topics.reason: QAC and valency evidence support a Form I perfect with no stated complement, matching the CRITICAL claim of settled absolute rejection.

topics.headline: covering pressure exposed by mirage
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the covering/concealment range becoming visible in a scene where deceptive appearance is finally exposed.
topics.reason: The covering image survives as lexical pressure, but the local selected sense remains disbelief/rejection rather than an agricultural or merely physical act.

topics.headline: voided-deeds pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this verb joining a Quranic pattern where disbelieving action and deeds are paired with futility (14:18; 18:103-105; 24:39).
topics.reason: The inter-ayah and boundary rows give concrete patterning without overriding the local parse.

words.gloss_range: plural possessed deeds or outputs functioning as the subject of the mirage predicate
words.root_gloss_range: doing, working, producing, and moral action; locally the possessed body of deeds is evaluated as mirage-like
words.prose: {{ar:أَعْمَٰلُهُمْ}} ({{tr:aʿmāluhum}}) makes the group’s own accumulated deeds the grammatical subject. The predicate does not compare the people vaguely to a desert; it reclassifies their owned output as mirage-like. The same work-root has just carried rewarded action in 24:38, so the boundary makes the reversal exact: selected and increased deeds there, emptied deeds here, within the wider voided-deeds pattern of ashes (14:18), weightlessness (18:105), and nullification (47:8-9).

topics.headline: owned deeds as grammatical subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the deeds themselves, specifically owned by the group, are what the simile evaluates.
topics.reason: The noun is the nominal subject with a possessive suffix, and the comparison phrase is its predicate.

topics.headline: plural body of outputs
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the verdict covering a gathered body of actions and outputs rather than one isolated deed.
topics.reason: The plural and root range support moral deeds, labor, and produced output, all locally gathered under the mirage predicate.

topics.headline: reward-to-nullity inversion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same work-root moving from rewarded deeds in 24:38 to mirage-deeds in 24:39, with opposite outcomes.
topics.reason: The boundary rows make the adjacent inversion central: reward and bounty give way to declarative nullification.

words.gloss_range: comparison preposition governing the mirage noun and opening the extended simile
words.prose: {{ar:كَ}} ({{tr:ka}}) turns the predicate into explicit comparison. Because it governs the mirage noun directly, the abstract subject of deeds is carried into a full test-scene: apparent value, pursuit, collapse, encounter, and accounting.

topics.headline: explicit simile governor
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the comparison is grammatically marked, not left as a loose metaphor.
topics.reason: The particle governs the mirage noun and attaches as a proclitic, making the likeness claim explicit.

topics.headline: extended parable hinge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a small comparison particle opening a full scene with perception, arrival, non-finding, God-finding, and reckoning.
topics.reason: The rows show the particle as the hinge from nominal predication into an extended narrative test.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive mirage used as the simile vehicle and specified by flat terrain
words.root_gloss_range: flowing, slipping away, hidden passage, and mirage; locally the mirage sense is selected with vanishing pressure
words.prose: {{ar:سَرَابٍ}} ({{tr:sarābin}}) supplies the vehicle: an indefinite ground-level mirage governed by the comparison and then placed in flat terrain. Its root pressure of flowing away and slipping beneath the surface makes the promised substance feel visually present yet materially unreachable. The rare term also links the dissolution of deeds here with mountains becoming mirage (78:20), while the sibilant-liquid sound suits the image’s shimmer.

topics.headline: specified mirage vehicle
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the vehicle is an indefinite mirage specifically located in flat terrain, not illusion in general.
topics.reason: The noun is genitive after the comparison particle and locally specified by the following terrain phrase.

topics.headline: vanishing and flow pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a ground-level shimmer whose apparent flow or substance slips away at contact.
topics.reason: The root field of flowing, departing, and hidden passage survives as image pressure, narrowed by the local noun to mirage.

topics.headline: rare dissolution echo
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the marked mirage term linking human deeds in 24:39 with cosmic dissolution in 78:20.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows give concrete distribution evidence and a 78:20 echo, kept as analogy rather than local sense control.

topics.headline: slipping sound texture
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sibilant-liquid sound reinforcing the unstable shimmer of the image.
topics.reason: The phonetic rows provide a local sound-form payoff tied directly to the surface word.

words.gloss_range: locative phrase naming flat exposed terrain where the mirage appears
words.root_gloss_range: patch, spot, marked ground, and flat open expanse; locally the flat barren terrain sense is active
words.prose: {{ar:بِقِيعَةٍ}} ({{tr:bi-qīʿatin}}) places the mirage on the kind of exposed flat where the deception can happen. The terrain pressure is concrete: patchy, barren, sun-open ground makes the visual promise of water environmentally credible and materially false. The singular concentrates the scene, while the plural reading broadens the same barren field without changing the parable’s mechanism.

topics.headline: locative terrain setting
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the terrain is a necessary condition for the mirage, not decorative scenery.
topics.reason: The locative preposition and singular terrain noun place the mirage in the flat setting that makes the image plausible.

topics.headline: barren flat ground pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the false water appearing over exposed, patchy, barren ground rather than fertile land.
topics.reason: The root field of patchy or spotted ground survives as terrain coloring, narrowed by the local noun to flat mirage-ground.

topics.headline: variant breadth and rare terrain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the unusual terrain word sharply concentrating the parable, while the plural reading broadens the same barren setting.
topics.reason: The accepted variant can broaden the terrain field without changing the canonical local singular scene.

words.gloss_range: imperfect cognition verb with object suffix and predicate complement, meaning he reckons it to be water
words.root_gloss_range: supposing, considering, counting, reckoning, and accounting; locally false human reckoning is selected
words.prose: {{ar:يَحْسَبُهُ}} ({{tr:yaḥsabuhu}}) makes the error an act of reckoning. The imperfect sustains the misperception as the thirsty figure approaches, and the object suffix plus complement make a formal judgment: he classifies it as water. The accepted vowel variant keeps the pressure between supposing and calculating visible without changing that object relation. This is the first station of the ayah’s accounting arc, moving from suspended count in 24:38 to false human calculation, then to personal account and the final reckoning.

topics.headline: formal misperception construction
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the mirage is not merely seen; it is formally classified as water over time.
topics.reason: The imperfect cognition verb takes an object suffix and predicate complement, sustaining a false judgment until arrival.

topics.headline: supposition as reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices perception turning into calculation: the thirsty figure misreckons reality, not just mis-sees it.
topics.reason: The root range and accepted vowel variant keep supposing and computing jointly available in the local cognition verb.

topics.headline: false-to-true reckoning arc
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the first station of the ayah’s root arc: suspended count in 24:38 becomes human misreckoning, personal account, and final divine reckoning in 24:39.
topics.reason: The rows make the ḥ-s-b chain structural across the ayah and its boundary, so it must shape commentary.

words.gloss_range: definite qualitative adjective naming an intensely thirsty archetypal subject
words.root_gloss_range: thirst and parched deprivation; locally intense bodily need that distorts perception
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلظَّمْـَٔانُ}} ({{tr:al-ẓamʾānu}}) is not a neutral observer. The definite, intense thirst form makes need itself the perceiving subject, so the false water is desired before it is tested. The hamza and its smoothing variant make the word’s sound-shape feel marked, and the rare form also contrasts with thirst endured in God’s cause (9:120): the same bodily condition can become merit there and delusion here.

topics.headline: definite intense thirst figure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a recognizable, intensely thirsty figure whose bodily state drives the scene.
topics.reason: The definite article and adjective pattern support an archetypal figure in an acute state rather than a mild or neutral observer.

topics.headline: need distorts perception
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices thirst functioning epistemologically: bodily lack bends judgment toward the false water.
topics.reason: The lexical rows tie the thirst root directly to perception distortion in the mirage scene.

topics.headline: marked thirst contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this rare marked thirst form contrasting delusive thirst here with meritorious thirst in 9:120.
topics.reason: The recurrence, rarity, and variant rows preserve contrast and sound-form payoff without changing the local referent.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative water as the false predicate complement of reckoning
words.root_gloss_range: water, watery substance, and possible overlay/deception imagery; locally concrete water is selected as the false object of thirst
words.prose: {{ar:مَآءً}} ({{tr:māʾan}}) is the false predicate: the mirage is reckoned to be water. Local thirst keeps the sense concrete, while the root dispute and overlay/deception pressure add irony: the desired life-substance is only a surface claim. The same surah contrasts this illusory water with real life-origin water in 24:45.

topics.headline: water as false predicate
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices water functioning as the grammatical content of a false classification.
topics.reason: The accusative noun is the second object or predicate complement of the cognition verb.

topics.headline: water and surface-deception pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the sought life-substance carrying an added irony of surface overlay and deception, while the local sense remains concrete water.
topics.reason: The root dispute and Form II imagery are useful pressure, but local thirst selects concrete water as the object of false predication.

topics.headline: unique illusory water use
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices familiar real water becoming, in this ayah, the label for non-existent substance, in contrast with real life-origin water in 24:45.
topics.reason: The distribution and same-surah echo show a concrete contrast between false water in 24:39 and created-from-water life in 24:45.

words.gloss_range: temporal endpoint particle marking the limit of the mirage’s persuasive force
words.prose: {{ar:حَتَّىٰٓ}} ({{tr:ḥattā}}) sets the limit of illusion. The false reckoning can continue only up to the threshold of arrival, and the extended recitational surface audibly stretches that threshold; with the next particle it divides the scene into before-arrival appearance and after-arrival disclosure.

topics.headline: endpoint of illusion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the illusion lasting only up to a testing threshold.
topics.reason: The particle marks a temporal limit and joins with the following particle to frame the arrival point.

topics.headline: stretched pivot threshold
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the before/after hinge where perception becomes disclosure and judgment.
topics.reason: The sequence rows identify the particle pair as the structural fulcrum of the parable.

words.gloss_range: temporal/conditional adverb introducing the certain arrival event
words.prose: {{ar:إِذَا}} ({{tr:idhā}}) frames the decisive moment as when, not merely if. It opens the compact reversal sequence: arrival, failure to find the expected object, and finding God.

topics.headline: inevitable when-event
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the collapse of the illusion is framed as a when-event, not a remote possibility.
topics.reason: The temporal/conditional particle normally frames expected occurrence, and here it introduces the certain test-point.

topics.headline: three-verb reversal frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the particle opening the rapid sequence of approach, failed finding, and God-finding.
topics.reason: The sequence rows show this particle as the frame for the dramatic verb chain.

words.gloss_range: perfect arrival verb with object suffix, reaching the perceived target
words.root_gloss_range: coming and arrival; locally arrival at the mirage target as a decisive test
words.prose: {{ar:جَآءَهُۥ}} ({{tr:jāʾahu}}) makes the test-point arrive with completed force, matching the root’s Quranic pattern of perfect arrival. The suffix keeps the target identical with what had been reckoned as water, so the movement closes the distance that made the mirage persuasive.

topics.headline: certain completed arrival
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the future test-point being narrated with the force of completed arrival.
topics.reason: The perfect verb after the temporal particle gives the arrival accomplished force, consistent with the distributional evidence.

topics.headline: target continuity collapses distance
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that reaching the very target of perception destroys the distance on which the mirage depended.
topics.reason: The suffix keeps the perceived target continuous, and the arrival verb closes the distance that sustained the illusion.

words.gloss_range: jussive negation particle making the following finding verb a decisive past denial
words.prose: {{ar:لَمْ}} ({{tr:lam}}) makes the search fail decisively. It governs the following verb into jussive truncation, matching the thematic truncation of the search, and creates the negative pole of the reversal: first nothing is found, then God is found.

topics.headline: decisive jussive negation
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the non-finding expressed as decisive past negation with a formally governed verb.
topics.reason: The particle negates the following imperfect and governs its jussive form, producing categorical non-finding.

topics.headline: negative pole of reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this negation preparing the immediate contrast with the affirmed God-finding.
topics.reason: The rows locate the particle as the negative half of the paired finding clauses.

words.gloss_range: jussive negated finding verb with object suffix, denying the perceived target
words.root_gloss_range: finding, encountering, existence, and experience; locally negated finding becomes non-existence of the expected object
words.prose: {{ar:يَجِدْهُ}} ({{tr:yajidhu}}) tests the same target named by the suffix and finds it absent. Because the root can link finding with existence, the clause does more than deny water; it begins denying the mirage as a real object. The same root then returns affirmatively, making the reversal from no object to God present unmistakable.

topics.headline: negated finding of the target
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the exact perceived target is tested and denied, not merely delayed or partially missed.
topics.reason: The jussive verb under negation keeps the same object suffix and takes a complement that denies the target as any thing.

topics.headline: finding tied to existence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices non-finding becoming ontological denial: the mirage is not found as something that exists.
topics.reason: The w-j-d field supports finding, existence, and experience, all locally narrowed to a failed finding with ontological force.

topics.headline: negated then affirmed finding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the repeated root carrying the central reversal from expected object absent to God present.
topics.reason: The repeated finding verb is structural: the same root holds both negation and disclosure.

words.gloss_range: indefinite accusative thing/entity under negation, yielding nothing whatsoever
words.root_gloss_range: thingness, entity, object, and existent; locally exhaustive non-thingness under negation
words.prose: {{ar:شَيْـًۭٔا}} ({{tr:shayʾan}}) completes the collapse. Under negation, the indefinite word for thingness makes the result not merely no water but no entity whatsoever; the same broad scope word that can range across cosmic and legal statements in the surah is used here to erase the apparent object completely.

topics.headline: total non-thing complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the negation reaching beyond no water to no thing whatsoever.
topics.reason: The indefinite entity noun under negation supplies exhaustive ontological denial.

topics.headline: universal scope word erased here
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a broad same-surah scope word used here to erase the apparent object completely.
topics.reason: The recurrence row supports a same-surah scope contrast without adding a separate local sense.

words.gloss_range: coordinating conjunction linking negated finding to affirmed finding
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) is the hinge between the two finding clauses. It keeps the negated object-finding and the affirmed God-finding joined, so the reversal is syntactic as well as thematic.

topics.headline: reversal conjunction between findings
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices absence and presence forced into immediate syntactic juxtaposition.
topics.reason: The conjunction coordinates the negated finding clause with the affirmed finding clause and carries adversative reversal in context.

words.gloss_range: perfect finding verb taking God as direct object after the failed finding clause
words.root_gloss_range: finding, encountering, existence, and experience; locally accomplished encounter with God
words.prose: {{ar:وَجَدَ}} ({{tr:wajada}}) reverses the previous failure with a completed finding. The object is now God, so the root shifts from retrieval of a hoped-for resource to unavoidable encounter. The pattern also resonates with judgment disclosure in 39:47, where what people had not reckoned appears from God.

topics.headline: accomplished divine finding
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the encounter with God stated as a completed direct-object finding after the failed search.
topics.reason: The perfect verb takes the divine name as direct object, reversing the prior negated finding.

topics.headline: perception becomes encounter
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices finding shifting from retrieval of water to inescapable existential encounter.
topics.reason: The same root frame now has God as object, so the finding is encounter rather than acquisition.

topics.headline: unexpected divine disclosure parallel
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the judgment pattern of encountering from God what had not been reckoned (39:47).
topics.reason: The inter-ayah rows give a concrete 39:47 parallel and are kept as a contrastive apparatus point.

topics.headline: polarity and object reversal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same root flipping from negated mirage-finding to affirmed God-finding.
topics.reason: The echo rows preserve the core wordplay of repeated root, changed polarity, and changed object.

words.gloss_range: accusative proper divine name as direct object of the affirmed finding verb
words.root_gloss_range: deity, worship, and possible bewilderment derivation; locally the proper divine name as encountered reality
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهَ}} ({{tr:Allāha}}) is the reality found where water had been projected. Its accusative case makes the divine name the direct object of the same finding frame that failed over the mirage. The proper name’s definiteness sharpens the contrast: the apparent water loses identity, while God is uniquely encountered; the derivational pressure keeps worship and bewilderment live at the reversal point, and the same-surah water contrast with 24:45 keeps real life-origin water distinct from this illusion.

topics.headline: direct divine object at collapse point
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices God as the directly found reality at the very point where the mirage loses identity.
topics.reason: The proper divine name is accusative as direct object of the finding verb, not a detached comment.

topics.headline: real replaces projected water
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the expected water replaced by the uniquely definite divine name at the same scene-location.
topics.reason: The rows identify the substitution: projected water collapses and the divine reality is encountered.

topics.headline: derivation dispute and water contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices worship/bewilderment pressure around the divine name and the contrast between illusory water in 24:39 and created water in 24:45.
topics.reason: The derivational dispute remains interpretive pressure; it does not alter the local proper-name role.

words.gloss_range: locative adverb with suffix, at him/at it, marking the point of divine encounter
words.root_gloss_range: at, with, in the presence of, and possession/proximity; locally personal locative presence at the collapse point
words.prose: {{ar:عِندَهُۥ}} ({{tr:ʿindahu}}) localizes the encounter. The suffix makes the scene personal: God is found at his point of arrival, and the phrase can also hold the mirage-location as the place where illusion gives way to presence. That concentrated point is where finding, presence, and accounting converge.

topics.headline: personal locative presence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the encounter localized at the seeker’s own point of arrival, not left abstract.
topics.reason: The locative adverb with suffix attaches to the finding verb and routes the presence to the thirsty/disbelieving figure.

topics.headline: location and presence double reading
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase holding both the mirage-location and the man’s own presence as the place of encounter.
topics.reason: The pronoun ambiguity is locally meaningful and supported, but it stays within the same locative phrase.

topics.headline: presence and accounting converge
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the broad locative field concentrated into one personal point where divine presence and reckoning meet.
topics.reason: The co-occurrence and rarity rows support the phrase as a concentrated encounter point.

words.gloss_range: result conjunction marking immediate consequence after finding God
words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa}}) drives the encounter straight into settlement. Unlike the earlier conjunction that pivots between clauses, this particle accelerates the result: finding God immediately becomes receiving the account, preparing the final swift-reckoning coda.

topics.headline: immediate consequential sequence
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices settlement following the encounter without a narrative interval.
topics.reason: The particle marks result and immediate succession, prefixed directly to the settlement verb.

topics.headline: acceleration toward swift coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the contrast between the wa- reversal and the fa- acceleration into reckoning, preparing the swift-reckoning coda.
topics.reason: The sequence rows connect the particle’s immediacy to the later swift attribute and distinguish it from the prior conjunction.

words.gloss_range: Form II perfect verb with object suffix, meaning God fully settles him/his due
words.root_gloss_range: fulfilling, completing, paying in full, and taking in full; locally full account settlement
words.prose: {{ar:وَفَّىٰهُ}} ({{tr:waffāhu}}) makes God the active settler and the figure the recipient. The Form II completion force turns judgment into full settlement, with the person and his account bound together by suffix and object. The pattern belongs with other divine full-settlement contexts (3:57; 4:173; 11:15; 11:111; 46:19), while the preceding result particle and final coda make that full settlement immediate.

topics.headline: God actively settles the person’s account
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the person receiving settlement from God rather than controlling the accounting event.
topics.reason: The active perfect verb has God as subject, the person as object suffix, and the account noun as the completed due.

topics.headline: Form II full completion
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices judgment as full completion with nothing left outstanding.
topics.reason: The w-f-y family and Form II morphology support completion, paying in full, and taking in full, locally selected as full settlement.

topics.headline: divine settlement pattern
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the local act joining a broader divine waffā settlement pattern (3:57; 4:173; 11:15; 11:111; 46:19) and converging with immediacy and swift reckoning.
topics.reason: The recurrence rows give concrete references and the convergence row links particle, form, account, and coda.

words.gloss_range: possessed account object governed by the full-settlement verb
words.root_gloss_range: reckoning, account, computation, sufficiency, and settled due; locally his personal account
words.prose: {{ar:حِسَابَهُۥ}} ({{tr:ḥisābahu}}) names what is fully settled: his own account. The possessive suffix binds the reckoning to the one who had misreckoned the mirage, so what he falsely treated as sufficient is answered by an actually sufficient settlement. It is the middle station of the root arc: human false calculation, personal account settled, then the universal reckoning, with 24:38’s no-reckoning bounty standing just across the boundary.

topics.headline: personal account as completed object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that what is completed is his own account, not the mirage or an abstract process.
topics.reason: The noun is the object of the settlement verb and is made definite by the possessive suffix.

topics.headline: reckoning moves from estimation to settlement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the same root moving from false subjective calculation to objective divine accounting.
topics.reason: The ḥ-s-b semantic range of reckoning, account, computation, and sufficiency is locally focused on the settled account.

topics.headline: middle of threefold accounting chain
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices this word as the middle station between human misreckoning and universal divine reckoning, after 24:38’s no-reckoning bounty.
topics.reason: The echo and boundary rows make the threefold chain central to the ayah’s structure.

words.gloss_range: resumptive conjunction introducing the final nominal coda
words.prose: {{ar:وَ}} ({{tr:wa}}) shifts out of the event sequence into a connected coda. The parable has reached personal settlement; this conjunction now opens the general statement that turns the scene into a principle.

topics.headline: resumptive coda reset
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the discourse moving from the specific parable event to a connected general declaration.
topics.reason: The conjunction restarts a nominal sentence after the settlement while keeping it formally connected.

topics.headline: parable-to-principle coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final statement functioning as a maxim-like tail that universalizes the scene.
topics.reason: The rows explicitly identify the move from parable instance to tadhyīl coda.

words.gloss_range: nominative proper divine name as subject of the final nominal sentence
words.root_gloss_range: deity and worship; locally the proper divine name anchoring the swift-reckoning attribute
words.prose: {{ar:ٱللَّهُ}} ({{tr:Allāhu}}) becomes the subject of the final nominal sentence. The name that was found as object now anchors the closing attribute, so the encountered God is the judging God. The principle has been experienced in the parable before it is stated as stable predicate.

topics.headline: divine name as nominal subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices swift reckoning predicated of God as a stable attribute, not as an abstract speed claim.
topics.reason: The nominative divine name is the subject of a verbless sentence whose predicate is the swift-reckoning construct.

topics.headline: found object becomes coda subject
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the divine name first as encountered object, then as the subject of the closing principle.
topics.reason: The case change from accusative to nominative tracks the movement from encounter to doctrinal coda.

topics.headline: principle experienced before stated
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the reckoning principle being embodied in the desert scene before it is named in the coda.
topics.reason: The boundary row supports the scene-to-attribute movement without adding a separate parse.

words.gloss_range: qualitative adjective in construct, predicate of God and restricted to reckoning
words.root_gloss_range: speed, haste, racing, and rapid movement; locally stabilized as swift reckoning
words.prose: {{ar:سَرِيعُ}} ({{tr:sarīʿu}}) supplies the predicate quality and binds it to the next noun: the swiftness is specifically in reckoning. The haste root becomes a stable divine attribute, naming the no-delay movement already enacted by the encounter and settlement. As part of a recurring epithet (2:202; 3:19; 3:199; 5:4; 13:41; 14:51; 40:17), its tight cadence compresses speed and accounting into compact coda force.

topics.headline: swift predicate restricted to reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices divine swiftness specified by the construct phrase as swiftness in reckoning.
topics.reason: The adjective functions as predicate and is bound in iḍāfa to the reckoning noun.

topics.headline: zero-delay judgment attribute
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the motion/haste root stabilized into an attribute that names the no-interval settlement just enacted.
topics.reason: The lexical rows connect haste pressure with the earlier fa-sequence while the local form is a qualitative adjective.

topics.headline: formulaic compact coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the phrase as a recurring divine epithet (2:202; 3:19; 3:199; 5:4; 13:41; 14:51; 40:17) made locally compact at the mirage parable’s close.
topics.reason: The recurrence and cadence rows preserve formulaic and sound-form payoff while keeping the local coda function primary.

words.gloss_range: definite genitive reckoning completing the swift-reckoning construct
words.root_gloss_range: reckoning, account, computation, and evaluative settlement; locally the universal known reckoning
words.prose: {{ar:ٱلْحِسَابِ}} ({{tr:al-ḥisābi}}) completes the construct and defines the domain: reckoning. Its definite form turns the man’s personal account into the known universal reckoning, and the fixed coda seals the parable as a general principle. The final return of the accounting root answers the earlier false calculation and the prior ayah’s no-reckoning bounty with divine reckoning.

topics.headline: genitive domain of swiftness
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the final noun defining the precise domain of the divine predicate.
topics.reason: The genitive noun completes the construct phrase after the swift adjective.

topics.headline: universal definite reckoning
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the shift from his personal account to the known universal reckoning.
topics.reason: The definite article contrasts with the possessed account and names the comprehensive evaluative process.

topics.headline: fixed swift-reckoning formula and coda
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the personal parable being sealed as a general divine-attribute maxim.
topics.reason: The rows identify the formula and tadhyīl function that universalize the scene.

topics.headline: final return of accounting root
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah ending where it began lexically: false human reckoning answered by divine reckoning, across the 24:38 boundary.
topics.reason: The echo and boundary rows make the root triad and previous-ayah contrast central to closure.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The repeated ح س ب in `يحسبه`, `حسابه`, and `الحساب` (words 6, 19, 22), joined to `سراب` and `ماء`.
baseline_models.mechanism: One root first supplies the thirsty seeker's estimate and then God's completed reckoning. The mirage externalizes a private valuation: intended works look sufficient from within desire, but arrival transfers measure from projection to account.

activation_trace.role: Supposition supplies the seeker's provisional valuation, while the repeated root lets that estimate face its accounting homonym.
Counting and reckoning replace the seeker's estimate with an exact divine measure.
A water-like visual with no real water gives the estimate its false perceptual object.
Thirst supplies the need that makes the false estimate persuasive.

changed_reading.before: The works are compared generally to deeds that prove fruitless.
changed_reading.after: The simile stages a collision between two measurements: desire calculates apparent value, then God's account recalculates the same works without projection.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The antithetical sequence `لم يجده شيئا ووجد الله عنده` (words 13-17).
baseline_models.mechanism: The doubled finding construction holds the encounter-site constant while replacing its object: water resolves to no reportable thing, yet God is present at its very `there`. Nullification is therefore not empty absence but a forced change in what counts as real and present.

activation_trace.role: The same act of encountering first fails toward the desired object and then succeeds toward God.
Existence sharpens the contrast between the non-entity of the projected object and the actuality encountered there.
The general reportable `thing` is explicitly denied to the expected water.
Nearness and presence make God present at, not merely subsequent to, the failed object.

changed_reading.before: The seeker fails to find water and is then judged.
changed_reading.after: The same locus undergoes an ontological substitution: the desired thing disappears as a thing, while divine presence and settlement are what the seeker actually encounters.

baseline_models.mechanism: Covering, intentional action, a water-like gleam, and the water root's plating or `tamwih` branch combine into a surface mechanism. The works are not merely absent; they carry a convincing finish that presents them in a life-giving form while covering their lack of substance.

activation_trace.role: Covering supplies the concealment beneath the works' visible finish.
Purposeful action identifies the material being appraised, rather than an accidental illusion.
Plating one material with a water-like or precious surface supplies the mechanism of presenting a thing as other than its reality.
The mirage is the completed visual coating: a water-image running before the eye without water.

changed_reading.before: The works simply vanish at the moment of need.
changed_reading.after: The works function as coated value: purposeful activity bears a persuasive life-giving sheen, but arrival exposes the mismatch between finish and substance.

context_deltas.mechanism: The slander unit repeatedly contrasts human calculation with divine valuation. What is calculated as evil can be good (24:11), and what is calculated as light is immense `with God` (24:15). This makes the focus mirage a moral scale-error as well as an optical error: the seeker's `water` and the speakers' `lightness` are persuasive estimates overturned at divine presence.

activation_trace.role: Supposition opens an explicit reversal from a calculated evil to a stated good.
Supposition assigns light weight to speech circulating without knowledge.
Presence `with God` relocates the standard by which that speech is weighed.
Ease and lightness name the humanly assigned low weight that divine proximity reverses.
Magnitude and force supply the opposed divine valuation.
The focus closes the same valuation problem by replacing supposition with reckoning.

structural_cues: 24:11 opens the slander sequence with a reversal of what is calculated; 24:15 repeats `you calculate it` followed by `with God`.
The focus repeats the estimate-to-divine-presence movement and then names account twice.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the repeated ح س ب and `عند الله` contrasts; I infer that the earlier moral revaluations train the focus's estimate-to-account reversal. A live alternative is simple lexical recurrence without a shared scale mechanism.

changed_reading.before: The thirsty seeker's estimate is corrected only because the visible object is unreal.
changed_reading.after: The unreal object exemplifies a surah-wide failure of weighting: speech and works can feel light, good, or sufficient until divine presence supplies their actual magnitude and account.

context_deltas.mechanism: In 24:24, embodied witnesses disclose what people were doing; in 24:25, God pays their recompense in full and they know God as the manifest, reality-matching truth. The focus repeats purposeful works, full payment, and encounter with God. Settlement therefore does not merely follow disclosure: exact settlement is itself the event by which false appearance gives way to manifest reality.

activation_trace.role: Purposeful acts become the content disclosed by bodily testimony.
Testimony grounded in knowledge makes otherwise hidden action evidentiary.
Full payment without deficiency supplies the exact settlement repeated in the focus.
Reckoning and recompense identify what is paid in full.
Reality fixed against falsehood names both the due and God known through its settlement.
Manifest disclosure makes truth visible at the end of the evidentiary process.
The focus's full account reenacts the earlier disclosure-through-settlement mechanism.

structural_cues: 24:24 moves from works to witnesses; 24:25 moves from full recompense to knowing God as manifest truth.
24:39 moves from works through failed appearance to finding God and full account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies parallel work, full-payment, God, and disclosure sequences; I infer that settlement produces epistemic disclosure in the focus. The alternative is that knowing and payment are adjacent consequences rather than one mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Finding God initiates a punitive accounting after the mirage fails.
changed_reading.after: The completed account is also a disclosure procedure: it converts covered action into evidence and makes the real, rather than the projected thing, manifest.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediately preceding sequence speaks in an economy of trade, sale, works, recompense, increase, surplus gift, and provision `without account`. The focus then ends with a fully paid personal account. Juxtaposition creates two value regimes: faithful work is met by best recompense plus unmeasured surplus, while mirage-work reaches the closure of what its account actually contains.

activation_trace.role: Commerce and the pursuit of profit establish the value-setting register immediately before the focus.
Exchange for a price supplies the transactional background that faithful actors refuse to let dominate remembrance.
Purposeful works are the basis of the preceding recompense, directly matching the focus's subject.
Answering an act with its recompense establishes reciprocal payment.
Increase carries the reward beyond strict equivalence.
Surplus and remainder name the source of value beyond earned recompense.
`Without account` removes provision from a bounded measure just before the focus reinstates personal account.
The completed personal account provides the bounded counterpart to the preceding unmeasured increase.

structural_cues: 24:37-38 and 24:39 are adjacent and share works, God, and account language.
24:38 ends `without account`; 24:39 ends with `his account` and `swift in account`.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies adjacency and an explicit surplus/increase versus account contrast; I infer asymmetric economies of grace and exact closure. A live alternative is that `without account` means abundance without implying a contrastive settlement regime.

changed_reading.before: The final account is simply the punishment attached to worthless deeds.
changed_reading.after: The account closes a deliberately contrasted economy: apparent profit cannot generate surplus, whereas faithful work is answered by best recompense and increase beyond measure.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus sits between sourced illumination and layered occlusion. In 24:35, light has a lamp, glass, fuel, ignition, and divine guidance; in 24:40, broad water, covering waves, and stacked layers defeat sight. The mirage is a third optical state: neither true illumination nor invisibility, but positive visibility detached from a sustaining source.

activation_trace.role: Illumination supplies the sourced visibility against which the mirage's unsupported gleam is measured.
Ignition gives true displayed light a material causal chain.
The mirage supplies visible water-form without the water substance that would sustain the sight.
A deceptive plated surface explains how visibility can be positive yet materially false.
Vast actual water reverses the focus's open dry field and encloses the observer.
A covering laid over something supplies the first layer of visual blockage.
Interfolding disturbance multiplies the covers that make actual water unreadable.
Eye-sight fails under the stacked medium, contrasting with the mirage's overconfident sight.
The closing denial of light makes divine illumination the condition for reliable visibility.

structural_cues: The light parable at 24:35, mirage at 24:39, and layered darkness at 24:40 form a close sequence.
The focus uses an exposed flat; 24:40 uses enclosing depth and superposed covers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies three adjacent optical constructions and their material media; I infer a triptych of sourced sight, false sight, and blocked sight. They may instead be separate similitudes joined only by a broad guidance theme.

changed_reading.before: The mirage is a stand-alone image of visual deception.
changed_reading.after: The mirage is the middle failure-mode in an optical system: it is visibility without source, between divinely grounded illumination and visibility erased by layered media.

context_deltas.mechanism: After the mirage, 24:43 gives actual water a traceable production path as rain exits assembled cloud, and 24:45 makes water the material from which creatures are created and move. The focus's water-image has neither provenance nor output: it yields `no thing`. Applied to works, the defect is sterility, not merely invisibility.

activation_trace.role: Descending rain supplies actual water with a named material event rather than a visual likeness.
Emergence from inside the cloud gives rain an observable causal provenance.
Known water is the real material from which the verse's creatures are made.
Bringing created beings into existence supplies real water's generative outcome.
The general knowable thing is affirmed within divine creation, reversing the focus's `no thing`.
Repeated locomotion makes generated life visibly operative after its watery origin.
The focus's apparent water is a presenting surface rather than generative material.
`No thing` states the false water's zero output at arrival.

structural_cues: 24:43 narrates cloud assembly, rain emergence, and descent; 24:45 states creation from water.
24:39's apparent water is followed by `he did not find it a thing`, while 24:45 joins water to creatures and every thing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies real-water causal chains and the focus's zero-result water image; I infer that generativity is the diagnostic separating substance from sheen. The alternative is a purely perceptual contrast with no claim about the productivity of works.

changed_reading.before: The water proves absent when the thirsty seeker arrives.
changed_reading.after: The apparent water is exposed as non-generative: unlike rain and creature-forming water, mirage-work has no causal depth and brings no living or actionable thing into being.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later sequence identifies God as the destination, depicts people turning away when called to divine judgment, and denies that disbelievers can outrun or frustrate pursuit on earth. The focus's thirsty arrival is therefore redirected: the traveler thinks the endpoint is water, but the unavoidable endpoint is divine presence and adjudication.

activation_trace.role: Becoming toward an ultimate end makes Godward destination explicit.
Turning away supplies attempted evasion after a verbal claim of obedience.
A spoken summons bends the addressee toward God and His messenger.
Judgment between people identifies the destination as adjudicative rather than merely spatial.
A further false supposition concerns the disbelievers' ability to evade outcome.
Denial of truth identifies the same class whose works form the focus mirage.
Escape by outstripping pursuit is explicitly negated across the earth.
The stated final lodging closes the failed attempt to evade destination.
Arrival to the apparent object becomes the scene in which the actual endpoint is encountered.
God's presence at the endpoint prevents the failed water from leaving an empty destination.

structural_cues: 24:42 states the Godward destination; 24:47-50 stages withdrawal from a summons to judgment.
24:57 repeats supposition plus disbelievers and denies escape across the earth.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies destination, summons, attempted withdrawal, failed escape, and the focus's arrival; I infer one redirected journey mechanism. The alternative is that the focus's arrival is only internal to its simile and not linked to later legal summonses.

changed_reading.before: A mistaken traveler happens upon judgment after chasing a false endpoint.
changed_reading.after: The false endpoint cannot cancel the real one: every route through the apparent object terminates in the divine presence and judgment the later claimants try, unsuccessfully, to avoid.

context_deltas.mechanism: In 24:47-53, voiced belief and obedience are followed by turning away at judgment, then strenuous oaths to act are answered by the demand for recognizable obedience and the statement that God knows what they do. This supplies a social form of mirage-work: verbal performance resembles compliant action until an adjudicative summons tests whether it has operative substance.

activation_trace.role: Spoken assertion gives the apparent obedience its visible verbal surface.
Submission is claimed as an accomplished act before conduct tests it.
Turning away breaks the asserted continuity between speech and deed.
The summons supplies the practical test that calls the claim into action.
Adjudication is the testing situation before which the verbal surface collapses.
Distributed solemn oath intensifies the presentation of promised action without itself supplying the action.
Known obedience is demanded as actual submission rather than oath-display.
Purposeful deeds, known by God, are the operative substance against which the display is tested.
The focus's works receive the same arrival-test as the later claims of obedience.

structural_cues: 24:47 moves from `we believe and obey` to immediate withdrawal; 24:48 supplies the judgment test.
24:53 moves from emphatic oaths to `known obedience` and God's knowledge of actual works.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies claim, withdrawal, summons, oath, and known work; I infer that performative compliance is one concrete instance of work with mirage-like appearance. A live alternative is that these verses address hypocrisy without specifying the focus simile's mechanism.

changed_reading.before: Mirage-work is an unspecified stock of deeds with no final value.
changed_reading.after: One concrete form is performative action: speech and oath display the outline of obedience, but the display yields no operative deed when judgment calls it forward.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah's close says people are returned to God, who reports to them what they did and knows every thing. Read back into the focus, `he did not find it a thing` cannot mean the deeds disappeared from knowledge or record. What vanishes is the projected payoff or object; the works remain fully reportable and accountable.

activation_trace.role: Return carries people back to the endpoint from which their state and acts are disclosed.
Delivered report makes their acts explicit to them rather than allowing those acts to vanish.
Purposeful works persist as the content of the final report.
God's knowledge encompasses every reportable thing at the close.
Failed finding applies to the expected object, while the second finding initiates account.
The denied thing is locally the mirage-object, not an erasure of the works from divine report.

structural_cues: 24:64 closes the surah with return, report of works, and knowledge of every thing.
24:39 denies a thing at the mirage-site but immediately supplies God and a complete account.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies local object-negation and final exhaustive reporting; I infer a scope distinction between nonexistent payoff and persistent record. The alternative is to take `no thing` as a total value judgment while still conceding that valueless deeds remain known.

changed_reading.before: Finding nothing suggests that the deeds themselves have become wholly absent.
changed_reading.after: Nothingness belongs to the expected payoff, not the record: the works survive as fully known and reportable evidence even though their projected object has no existence.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because the packet's split mapping carries و ج د into form-distant ج د د branches for shore, level ground, and waterless land. It remains anchored in the two focus occurrences of و ج د and the explicit flat قِيعَة scene, but downstream prose should call it a packet-induced topographic resonance, not a lexical derivation or settled sense of `وجد`.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: `بقيعة ... لم يجده ... ووجد` joins a flat place to the packet's split inventory for the doubled finding root.

activation_trace.role: A spread, level place supplies the scene's explicit exposed surface.
A water-edge or shore oddly echoes the boundary the seeker expects the mirage to provide.
A level, hard face of earth doubles the explicit flat on which both findings occur.
Waterless land supplies a packet-resolved material counterpart to finding no water-thing.

changed_reading.before: The two acts of finding occur against a neutral desert background.
changed_reading.after: The split inventory makes the encounter-site itself resonate as false shore, level ground, and waterless land, so the doubled `finding` seems materially staged before it is semantically resolved.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the thirst root's branch for the span of a life and the fulfillment root's branch for taking the soul, neither of which is forced by the surface syntax. Both are focus-root branches and the `until, when he came` sequence supports a temporal endpoint, but downstream prose should frame this only as a secondary life-course model, not as disambiguation.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: `الظمآن ... حتى إذا جاءه ... فوفاه ... سريع` links thirst, an until-bound arrival, fulfillment, and speed.

activation_trace.role: The span from birth to death lets thirst function as an entire bounded life interval.
Arrival supplies the endpoint reached when that interval closes.
Taking the soul supplies an exploratory transition from completed life to completed account.
Speed collapses delay between reaching the endpoint and reckoning.

changed_reading.before: A thirsty traveler reaches a disappointing object and is promptly judged.
changed_reading.after: The travel can model a whole thirst-span of life: its desired endpoint fails at arrival, the soul is taken, and account follows without temporal refuge.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because 24:15's ه و ن is split-mapped to a م ه ن branch describing scant weak water that does not fecundate. The image remains anchored through the focus's false water, `no thing`, and the exact shared misvaluation sequence, but downstream prose should identify it as a non-dominant split-root activation rather than the ordinary meaning of `هينا`.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus's water-like works yield `no thing`; 24:15 says a harmful utterance is calculated `light` while immense with God.

activation_trace.role: Scant weak water unable to fecundate turns the supposedly light utterance into an image of sterile liquidity.
Supposition supplies the false low valuation that licenses the weak-water resonance.
Water-like plating supplies the focus's corresponding surface without productive substance.
Failure to yield any thing gives the weak-water image its functional endpoint.

changed_reading.before: The slander's `lightness` and the mirage's water are separate images of error.
changed_reading.after: The split branch lets them meet as sterile liquidity: speech or work may circulate with a water-like surface while being wrongly discounted and unable to generate a real thing.

strongest_changes: The repeated `calculate ... with God` construction in 24:11-15 turns the mirage from mere optical failure into a failure of moral weight and measure.
24:24-25 makes full settlement a disclosure procedure, while 24:37-39 contrasts unmeasured surplus with a closed personal account.
The light, mirage, darkness, rain, and creature-from-water sequence distinguishes sourced and generative media from unsupported visual surface.
24:42, 24:47-57, and 24:64 make the seeker's arrival an unavoidable Godward return in which nonexistent payoff coexists with a fully live record.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context did not merely repeat a theme. It interlocked exact lexical pivots across optical, juridical, economic, hydrological, and performative mechanisms, allowing several changed readings of the same focus construction to coexist.
remaining_uncertainties: The ج د د topography under the split و ج د mapping may be packet-induced resonance rather than useful semantic pressure.
The `without account` versus `his account` adjacency may contrast grace with exact closure, or may only juxtapose two descriptions of divine recompense.
The light-mirage-darkness sequence strongly supports an optical triptych, but the three images can still be read as locally independent similitudes.
Applying real water's generativity to the productivity of works requires a reader-supplied causal analogy.

reader_a.activated_readings_md: 1. **The mirage is a failed act of accounting corrected by a complete account.** **Lexical evidence:** fixed-ayah `س ر ب` B009 is mirage shimmering like water; `ق و ع` B001 is level spread-out ground; `ح س ب` B002 is supposition and B001 accounting; `ظ م ء` B001 is thirst; `و ج د` B001 is finding; `و ف ي` B001 is full completion. **Structural cue:** the grammar mirrors `يحسبه` with `حسابه` and `لم يجده` with `وجد الله`; 24:35 has distinguished guiding light, 24:38 provision beyond account, and 24:40 compounds failed visibility from the opposite direction. **Assigned role:** thirst biases the initial estimate, flat reflective ground supplies misleading evidence, and encounter replaces supposed object with the true accountant. **Abductive move:** the packet supplies desire, appearance, misclassification, nonfinding, and full reckoning; I infer motivated perception → false valuation → unavoidable audit. **Reading change:** the image diagnoses an epistemic-economic error: works are treated as liquid assets but yield nothing when settled.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 24:40 supplied the inverse failure to the mirage: one eye sees a nonexistent asset, the other cannot distinguish its own hand. 24:44 then turned both into a lesson about reversals of perception.

baseline.text: İnkâr edenlerin yaptıkları, düz bir arazideki serap gibidir. Susayan onu su sanır; yanına vardığında hiçbir şey bulamaz ve Allah'ı yanında bulur. Allah da hesabını eksiksiz görür. Allah hesabı çabuk görendir.

findings.text: Susuzluk, görünür parıltıyı işe yarar su olarak yorumlar; hakikatin örtülmesi boşluk değil, ihtiyacın gerçek sanacağı sahte bir hareket hedefi üretir.
Seraba varıldığında nesne kaybolur ve arayan kendisini Allah'ın eksiksiz hesabının yanında bulur; temsil temasla sınanırken arayan da hesabın konusu olur.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_semantic_invariant: Perception fails either because a false object occupies the desired object's visual place or because successive coverings absorb the path between observer and object.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.parent_surprising_reach: The branches separate optical resemblance, motivated projection, failed retrieval, exact accounting, vertical occlusion, and near-but-blocked recognition.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Mirage Substitutes for Water
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: A thirsty observer on an open plain takes a shimmering surface for water because visual resemblance meets urgent desire.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: mirage appearing as water `quranic:root_000691:B009/m01`; flat open ground `quranic:root_001270:B001/m01`; bodily thirst `quranic:root_000968:B001/m01`; longing for encounter figured as thirst `quranic:root_000968:B003/m01`; actual water `quranic:root_001458:B001/m01`; crystalline or mirror-like water clarity `quranic:root_001458:B007/m01`; supposition formed in the mind `quranic:root_000318:B002/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: Misperception is jointly produced by surface and observer. The plain supplies shimmer, water-like clarity supplies resemblance, thirst supplies the projected completion, and supposition closes the gap. The false object is visually present but materially absent.

channel_subchannels_anchored_here.name: Arrival Converts Search into Account
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.scene_or_process: The seeker reaches the expected site, fails to retrieve the projected object, encounters the actual authority there, and receives a fully settled account.
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.active_motifs: coming to a place or outcome `quranic:root_000281:B001/m01`; finding or failing to find an object `quranic:root_001626:B001/m01`; water as sought object `quranic:root_001458:B001/m01`; complete settlement without remainder `quranic:root_001669:B001/m01`; counting and reckoning `quranic:root_000318:B001/m01`; speed opposed to delay `quranic:root_000698:B001/m01`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.ayah_anchors: 24:39 `حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءَهُ لَمْ يَجِدْهُ شَيْئًا وَوَجَدَ اللَّهَ عِندَهُ فَوَفَّاهُ حِسَابَهُ وَاللَّهُ سَرِيعُ الْحِسَابِ`
channel_subchannels_anchored_here.synthesis: The mirage scene ends as a retrieval and settlement scene. Arrival cancels the imagined object, but not encounter itself; the empty visual promise is replaced by exact, immediate accounting. Failure to find is therefore a transition into being found and measured.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi, bir şeyi örtme ve görünmez kılma çekirdeğini; zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme, külün toprakla kapanması ve yıldızların güneş ışığında görünmemesi gibi gerçekleşmelerle açıkça destekler.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Çekirdek fiziksel örtmedir; dinî inkâr, nimeti yadsıma ve günahı giderme bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım yalın örtme çekirdeğini korur; zırh, silah, kül ve gök cisimleriyle ilgili kullanımlar bu çekirdeğin yapıya bağlı gerçekleşmeleri olarak ayrılır.

concept_map.definition: Bir şeyi başka bir şeyle örterek görünmesini engellemek veya kapalı duruma getirmektir. Zırhın giysiyle, kişinin silahla ya da külün savrulan toprakla örtülmesi bu işlemin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.

facets.statement: Bir nesnenin üstünü kapatarak onu görünmez veya örtülü duruma getirme işlemi.
Zırhı giysiyle kaplama, silahla örtünme ve külün üstünün toprakla kapanması çekirdeğin özel gerçekleşmeleridir.
Güneşin yıldızları görünmez kılması da görsel örtme sonucu üzerinden bu çekirdeğe bağlanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar örtme ve kapatma çekirdeğinde birleşir; farklı örnekler bu işlemin nesne, giysi, silah, kül ve gök görünümü üzerindeki gerçekleşmelerini gösterir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Bir şeyin üstünü başka bir şeyle kapatıp görünmesini engelleyen genel çekirdek için uygundur.

error_profile.preserves: Örtme işlemini ve görünürlüğün engellenmesi sonucunu birlikte korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Zırhın giysiyle veya külün toprakla kaplanması gibi somut bağlamlarda doğal bir karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Somut bir nesnenin üstünün kapatılması işlemini eksiksiz korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Güneş ışığının yıldızları görünmez kıldığı göksel bağlamda sonuç odaklı doğal karşılıktır.

error_profile.preserves: Görsel örtmenin görünürlüğü ortadan kaldıran sonucunu korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi karanlık geceyi, denizi, büyük ırmağı, gün batımını ve bulutu aynı adlandırma çevresinde toplar; bunların tümünü tek bir gerçek 'kuşatan örtü' türü saymak yerine, karanlık, genişlik veya kapatma etkisiyle örten farklı varlıklar olarak anlamak gerekir.

lexicalization_scope.note: Yalın dal, kaynakta doğrudan adlandırılan gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı ve bulut kapsamıyla tanımlanır; yapıya özgü başka anlam eklenmez.

concept_map.definition: Karanlığı, genişliği veya kapatma etkisi nedeniyle kişileri ya da görünümü örten karanlık gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı veya bulut için kullanılan bir nitelemedir.

facets.statement: Karanlık, genişlik ya da kapatma etkisiyle başka şeylerin görünmesini veya seçilmesini engelleyen varlık.
Gece, deniz, büyük ırmak, gün batımı ve bulut kaynaklarda bu nitelemenin farklı gönderimleri olarak sıralanır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Kaynaklar aynı sözü karanlık gece, deniz ve büyük ırmak için verir; bazı aktarımlar gün batımını ve bulutu da örtücü etkileri nedeniyle bu listeye ekler.
